summary: The study investigates the plasma-enhanced atomic layer deposition (PEALD) of tungsten nitride (WN) using bis(tert-butylimido)bis(dimethylamido)tungsten (BTBMW) as the precursor and N2, H2=N2, and NH3 plasmas. The process was evaluated over a temperature range of 100–400 /C14 C. The lowest resistivity film, 405 lX cm, was achieved at 400 /C14 C with a hydrogen-rich H2=N2 plasma. The study highlights the impact of process parameters on film growth rate, optical properties, composition, and resistivity.
evidence: Tungsten nitride (WN) has potential as an interconnect barrier film.
